title: User and Entity Behavior Analytics — Anomalous Process Execution (MLTK)

dataSources: `index=endpoint sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational` (EventCode=1) Collected via Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (Splunkbase 742) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
app: Splunk Machine Learning Toolkit (MLTK), Splunk Enterprise Security (ES), Sysmon TA — Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (Splunkbase 742)
spl:
| tstats `security_content_summariesonly` count FROM datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    BY _time span=1d, Processes.dest, Processes.process_name, Processes.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| eventstats dc(dest) as host_prevalence by process_name
| eventstats avg(count) as user_avg stdev(count) as user_std by dest, process_name
| eval rarity_score=1 - (host_prevalence / max_hosts)
| eval z_score=round((count - user_avg) / nullif(user_std, 0), 2)
| where (rarity_score > 0.95 OR z_score > 3) AND count < 5
| fit DensityFunction count by dest into process_anomaly_model
| where isOutlier > 0
| lookup asset_lookup dest OUTPUT priority, bunit, category
| table _time, dest, user, process_name, count, rarity_score, z_score, priority
| sort -rarity_score
description: Establishing per-host baselines of normal process execution and flagging rare or never-before-seen processes catches fileless malware, living-off-the-land binaries (LOLBins), and novel toolkits that signature-based EDR misses.
value: Early 'User and Entity Behavior Analytics — Anomalous Process Execution (MLTK)' detection reduces missed threat campaigns, control regressions, and SOC SLA breaches by giving Security Infra operators a Splunk-native signal before manual triage or audit channels surface the issue.
implementation: Collect Sysmon Event ID 1 (process creation) and build a 30-day baseline of process-to-host mappings. Calculate host prevalence (how many hosts run this process) and per-host execution frequency. Processes that appear on fewer than 5% of hosts and have unusually high or first-time execution counts are flagged. Use DensityFunction for multivariate outlier detection across count and prevalence. Enrich with asset criticality from ES. Feed as risk events with MITRE T1059 annotation. Exclude known deployment tools (SCCM, Puppet, Chef) via a managed allowlist. Review and update the allowlist monthly.
visualization: Table (rare processes with rarity score), Scatter plot (rarity vs z-score), Bar chart (top anomalous hosts).
knownFalsePositives:
1. **Approved vulnerability scanner** — Scanner `src` triggers high-severity signatures for 'User and Entity Behavior Analytics — Anomalous Process Execution (MLTK)'. Join `scanner_ips` before threshold.

2. **Signature definition update** — Vendor content push reclassifies benign traffic. Compare threat_id first_seen with content release date.

3. **Red-team emulation** — Atomic test traffic from approved exercise hosts.

4. **Backup replication traffic** — Off-hours bulk transfer matches lateral-movement heuristics.

**Suppression mechanism:** `soc_exception_register.csv` keyed on `src`, `threat_id`, `valid_until`.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Install and configure the required add-on or app: Splunk Machine Learning Toolkit (MLTK), Splunk Enterprise Security (ES), Sysmon TA.
• Ensure the following data sources are available: `index=endpoint sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational` (EventCode=1).
• For app installation, inputs.conf, and Splunk directory layout, see the Implementation guide: docs/implementation-guide.md

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Collect Sysmon Event ID 1 (process creation) and build a 30-day baseline of process-to-host mappings. Calculate host prevalence (how many hosts run this process) and per-host execution frequency. Processes that appear on fewer than 5% of hosts and have unusually high or first-time execution counts are flagged. Use DensityFunction for multivariate outlier detection across count and prevalence. Enrich with asset criticality from ES. Feed as risk events with MITRE T1059 annotation. Exclude known de…

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
| tstats `security_content_summariesonly` count FROM datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    BY _time span=1d, Processes.dest, Processes.process_name, Processes.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| eventstats dc(dest) as host_prevalence by process_name
| eventstats avg(count) as user_avg stdev(count) as user_std by dest, process_name
| eval rarity_score=1 - (host_prevalence / max_hosts)
| eval z_score=round((count - user_avg) / nullif(user_std, 0), 2)
| where (rarity_score > 0.95 OR z_score > 3) AND count < 5
| fit DensityFunction count by dest into process_anomaly_model
| where isOutlier > 0
| lookup asset_lookup dest OUTPUT priority, bunit, category
| table _time, dest, user, process_name, count, rarity_score, z_score, priority
| sort -rarity_score
```

Understanding this SPL

**User and Entity Behavior Analytics — Anomalous Process Execution (MLTK)** — Establishing per-host baselines of normal process execution and flagging rare or never-before-seen processes catches fileless malware, living-off-the-land binaries (LOLBins), and novel toolkits that signature-based EDR misses.

Documented **Data sources**: `index=endpoint sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational` (EventCode=1). **App/TA** (typical add-on context): Splunk Machine Learning Toolkit (MLTK), Splunk Enterprise Security (ES), Sysmon TA. The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

**Detection type** for this use case: endpoint — interpret thresholds and fields in that context.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Uses `tstats` against accelerated summaries for data model `Endpoint.Processes` — enable acceleration for that model.
• Invokes macro `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` — in Search, use the UI or expand to inspect the underlying SPL.
• `eventstats` rolls up events into metrics; results are split **by process_name** so each row reflects one combination of those dimensions.
• `eventstats` rolls up events into metrics; results are split **by dest, process_name** so each row reflects one combination of those dimensions.
• `eval` defines or adjusts **rarity_score** — often to normalize units, derive a ratio, or prepare for thresholds.
• `eval` defines or adjusts **z_score** — often to normalize units, derive a ratio, or prepare for thresholds.
• Filters the current rows with `where (rarity_score > 0.95 OR z_score > 3) AND count < 5` — typically the threshold or rule expression for this monitoring goal.
• Pipeline stage (see **User and Entity Behavior Analytics — Anomalous Process Execution (MLTK)**): fit DensityFunction count by dest into process_anomaly_model
• Filters the current rows with `where isOutlier > 0` — typically the threshold or rule expression for this monitoring goal.
• Enriches events using `lookup` (lookup definition + optional OUTPUT fields).
• Pipeline stage (see **User and Entity Behavior Analytics — Anomalous Process Execution (MLTK)**): table _time, dest, user, process_name, count, rarity_score, z_score, priority
• Orders rows with `sort` — combine with `head`/`tail` for top-N patterns.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare a handful of scored rows to **the MLTK experiment** that produced the model, or to a manual replay of the same SPL on a short window, and confirm `fit` / `apply` output matches. For side-by-side, compare notable or entity context to **the ES Incident Review** queue if you feed risk or tickets.



Step 4 — Operationalize
Add the search to a dashboard or set up alert actions (email, webhook, PagerDuty, etc.) as required. Document the use case in your runbook and assign an owner. Consider visualizations: Table (rare processes with rarity score), Scatter plot (rarity vs z-score), Bar chart (top anomalous hosts).

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (Splunk Machine Learning Toolkit (MLTK), Splunk Enterprise Security (ES), Sysmon TA — Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (Splunkbase 742)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=see SPL into index=main. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`Processes.dest, Processes.process_name, Processes.user, _time`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
